GSEA for gene signatures significantly changed between W0 and W16 in the treatment successful group (Figure 3C)

1 Introduction

Figure 3C: pathway activity changes between W0 and W16 in patients with successful treatment outcome, adjusted for Age, Sex, and trial Arm. Cross-validation by NanoTube and PLAGE.

NanoTube limmaToFGSEA with a combined gene set of NanoString panel annotations and the Hallmark collection is the primary analysis. NanoString panel annotations capture the immune biology curated specifically for this panel. The Hallmark collection is added to cover the 30 additional customised genes in this panel that extend beyond the standard NanoString pathway annotations. Because Age, Sex, and trial Arm are patient-level variables that are collinear with the donor blocking factor in a paired design, their effects are removed by residualising gene expression within each stimulation condition prior to analysis. Genes are then ranked by the limma paired t-statistic from a model of the form residualised expression ~ Donor + Visit. Significant pathways are defined as FDR < 0.01. Results are clustered by leading edge similarity.

PLAGE with the combined NanoString and Hallmark pathway set is used for validation. It computes a per-sample pathway activity score using the first principal component of the residualised pathway gene expression matrix, then tests the score with a paired t-test matched by donor. Because PLAGE uses a fundamentally different algorithm it provides independent confirmation of the primary results. Pathways that are significant in both analyses are considered the most robust findings and reported in the manuscript.

5 Filter and recode

One barcode (0408230288) is excluded as a quality control outlier. Stimulation labels are standardised to match the protein data naming convention.

nano_data <- all_data %>%
  filter(Comments == "success") %>%
  mutate(
    Stimulation = ifelse(Stimulation == "TB",   "Mtb_Ag", Stimulation),
    Stimulation = ifelse(Stimulation == "NULL", "Null",   Stimulation),
    Visit       = paste0("W", Visit)
  ) %>%
  filter(!Barcode %in% "0408230288") %>%
  select(-Barcode)

cat(sprintf("Rows: %d | Columns: %d\n", nrow(nano_data), ncol(nano_data)))
Rows: 231 | Columns: 842
cat(sprintf("Visits: %s\n",       paste(unique(nano_data$Visit),       collapse = ", ")))
Visits: W0, W16
cat(sprintf("Stimulations: %s\n", paste(unique(nano_data$Stimulation), collapse = ", ")))

nano_data <- nano_data %>%
  mutate(
    Age = as.numeric(Age),
    Sex = factor(Sex, levels = c("Female", "Male")),
    Arm = factor(Arm, levels = c("A", "B", "C"))
  )

cat(sprintf("Covariate check - Age range: %.0f - %.0f | Sex levels: %s | Arm levels: %s\n",

7 Define gene columns

Gene columns run from ACE to TBP. A guard check stops the document if either boundary column is missing.

col_start <- which(names(nano_data) == "ACE")
col_end   <- which(names(nano_data) == "TBP")

if (length(col_start) == 0 || length(col_end) == 0) {
  stop("ACE or TBP not found in nano_data. Check column names.")
}

gene_cols <- names(nano_data)[col_start:col_end]

cat(sprintf(
  "First gene: %s | Last gene: %s | Total: %d\n",
  names(nano_data)[col_start],
  names(nano_data)[col_end],
  length(gene_cols)
))

8 Load NanoString pathway annotations

The NanoString immune panel includes its own pathway annotations for each probe. The annotation column uses :: as a separator between multiple pathway assignments.

probe_annot <- read_csv(input_annot, show_col_types = FALSE)

nanostring_pathway_df <- probe_annot %>%
  filter(Is.Control == 0,
         !is.na(Probe.Annotation),
         Probe.Annotation != "") %>%
  select(Gene = Probe.Label, Pathway = Probe.Annotation) %>%
  separate_rows(Pathway, sep = "::") %>%
  filter(!is.na(Pathway), Pathway != "")

nanostring_pathways <- split(nanostring_pathway_df$Gene,
                             nanostring_pathway_df$Pathway)

cat(sprintf("NanoString-defined pathways: %d\n", length(nanostring_pathways)))
NanoString-defined pathways: 57
pathway_coverage <- sapply(nanostring_pathways, function(g) sum(g %in% gene_cols))

cat(sprintf(
  "Pathways with at least 3 genes measured: %d / %d\n",
  sum(pathway_coverage >= 3),
  length(nanostring_pathways)
))
Pathways with at least 3 genes measured: 57 / 57

9 Load Hallmark gene sets

Only Hallmark gene sets with at least 3 genes measured in this panel are retained to avoid testing pathways with minimal representation.

hallmark <- msigdbr(species = "Homo sapiens", collection = "H") %>%
  select(gs_name, gene_symbol)

hallmark_list <- split(hallmark$gene_symbol, hallmark$gs_name)

hallmark_filtered <- hallmark_list[
  sapply(hallmark_list, function(g) sum(g %in% gene_cols) >= 3)
]

cat(sprintf(
  "Hallmark gene sets with at least 3 genes measured: %d / %d\n",
  length(hallmark_filtered),
  length(hallmark_list)
))
Hallmark gene sets with at least 3 genes measured: 46 / 50

10 Build combined pathway set

NanoString panel annotations are merged with the filtered Hallmark collection. Duplicate names are removed.

combined_pathways <- c(nanostring_pathways, hallmark_filtered)
combined_pathways <- combined_pathways[!duplicated(names(combined_pathways))]

cat(sprintf(
  "Combined pathway set: %d NanoString + %d Hallmark = %d total\n",
  length(nanostring_pathways),
  length(hallmark_filtered),
  length(combined_pathways)
))
Combined pathway set: 57 NanoString + 46 Hallmark = 103 total

11 Residualise expression against covariates

Age, Sex, and Arm cannot be included directly in the paired design matrix because they are patient-level variables that are collinear with the Donor blocking factor. Instead, the effect of these covariates is removed from gene expression values before the paired analysis. Residualisation is performed separately within each stimulation condition. The residuals carry the covariate-adjusted variation and are used in all downstream analyses.

residualise_expression <- function(data, gene_cols,
                                   covariates = c("Age", "Sex", "Arm")) {

  data %>%
    group_by(Stimulation) %>%
    group_modify(function(stim_data, key) {

      missing_cov <- sum(!complete.cases(stim_data[, covariates, drop = FALSE]))
      if (missing_cov > 0) {
        cat(sprintf("  Warning: %d rows with missing covariate values in %s\n",
                    missing_cov, key$Stimulation))
      }

      cov_formula <- as.formula(paste("gene_val ~", paste(covariates, collapse = " + ")))

      for (gene in gene_cols) {
        fit_data        <- stim_data
        fit_data$gene_val <- stim_data[[gene]]

        fit <- tryCatch(
          lm(cov_formula, data = fit_data),
          error = function(e) NULL
        )

        if (!is.null(fit)) {
          stim_data[[gene]] <- residuals(fit)
        }
      }
      stim_data
    }) %>%
    ungroup()
}

nano_data_resid <- residualise_expression(nano_data, gene_cols)

cat(sprintf(
  "Residualised dataset: %d rows | %d columns\n",
  nrow(nano_data_resid), ncol(nano_data_resid)
))
Residualised dataset: 231 rows | 842 columns

12 limma paired analysis

prepare_limma_data: filters to a given stimulation and visit pair, identifies paired donors, and returns a genes-by-samples expression matrix for limma.

prepare_limma_data <- function(data, stimulation, gene_cols,
                               visit_pair = c("W0", "W16")) {

  stim_data <- data %>%
    filter(Stimulation == stimulation, Visit %in% visit_pair)

  paired_donors <- stim_data %>%
    group_by(Donor) %>%
    summarise(
      has_W0  = any(Visit == "W0"),
      has_W16 = any(Visit == "W16"),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) %>%
    filter(has_W0 & has_W16) %>%
    pull(Donor)

  cat(sprintf("  %s: %d paired donors\n", stimulation, length(paired_donors)))

  if (length(paired_donors) < 3) {
    cat(sprintf("  Skipping %s: fewer than 3 paired donors\n", stimulation))
    return(NULL)
  }

  paired_data <- stim_data %>%
    filter(Donor %in% paired_donors) %>%
    arrange(Donor, Visit)

  expr_matrix <- paired_data %>%
    select(all_of(gene_cols)) %>%
    t()

  colnames(expr_matrix) <- paste(paired_data$Donor, paired_data$Visit, sep = "_")

  metadata <- data.frame(
    Sample = colnames(expr_matrix),
    Donor  = factor(paired_data$Donor),
    Visit  = factor(paired_data$Visit, levels = visit_pair),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )

  cat(sprintf("  Expression matrix: %d genes x %d samples\n",
              nrow(expr_matrix), ncol(expr_matrix)))

  list(expr_matrix = expr_matrix, metadata = metadata,
       n_donors = length(paired_donors))
}

13 Run limma for all stimulations

Limma results and ranked gene lists are saved and used by both NanoTube and PLAGE.

stimulations  <- unique(nano_data$Stimulation)
limma_fits    <- list()
limma_data    <- list()
limma_results <- list()

for (stim in stimulations) {
  data_prep <- prepare_limma_data(nano_data_resid, stim, gene_cols)

  if (is.null(data_prep)) next

  design  <- model.matrix(~ Donor + Visit, data = data_prep$metadata)
  fit     <- lmFit(data_prep$expr_matrix, design)
  fit     <- eBayes(fit)
  limma_fits[[stim]] <- fit
  results <- topTable(fit, coef = "VisitW16", number = Inf, sort.by = "none")
  results$Gene <- rownames(results)

  ranked_genes <- sort(setNames(results$t, results$Gene), decreasing = TRUE)

  cat(sprintf(
    "  %s: %d genes | FDR < 0.01: %d\n | t range: [%.2f, %.2f]\n",
    stim, nrow(results),
    sum(results$adj.P.Val < 0.01, na.rm = TRUE),
    min(results$t), max(results$t)
  ))

  limma_data[[stim]]    <- data_prep
  limma_results[[stim]] <- list(ranked_genes = ranked_genes, results = results)

  write_xlsx(
    results %>%
      arrange(desc(abs(t))) %>%
      select(Gene, logFC, AveExpr, t, P.Value, adj.P.Val, B),
    file.path(output_limma, paste0(stim, "_limma_results.xlsx"))
  )

  write_xlsx(
    data.frame(
      Gene        = names(ranked_genes),
      t_statistic = as.numeric(ranked_genes),
      Rank        = seq_along(ranked_genes),
      stringsAsFactors = FALSE
    ),
    file.path(output_limma, paste0(stim, "_ranked_genes.xlsx"))
  )
}

14 NanoTube GSEA with combined pathway set (primary analysis)

For each stimulation, a paired design matrix is passed to runLimmaAnalysis. limmaToFGSEA is called with the combined NanoString and Hallmark pathway set. Results are clustered by leading edge similarity and saved to Excel.

nanotube_gsea_results <- list()

for (stim in names(limma_fits)) {

  cat(sprintf("\nNanoTube GSEA (primary): %s\n", stim))

  gsea_res <- tryCatch(
    limmaToFGSEA(
      limmaResults = limma_fits[[stim]],
      gene.sets    = combined_pathways,
      min.set      = 3,
      rank.by      = "t",
      skip.first   = TRUE
    ),
    error = function(e) { message("GSEA failed: ", e$message); NULL }
  )

  if (is.null(gsea_res)) next

  nanotube_gsea_results[[stim]] <- list(
    limma = limma_fits[[stim]],
    gsea  = gsea_res
  )

  # gsea_res is a named list with one entry per design matrix coefficient.
  # We access the VisitW16 entry which holds the treatment effect results.
  if (is.null(gsea_res[["VisitW16"]])) {
    cat(sprintf("  VisitW16 coefficient not found for %s. Check design matrix.\n", stim))
    next
  }

  l_edge <- tryCatch(
    fgseaToLEdge(
      gsea_res[["VisitW16"]],
      cutoff.type = "padj",
      cutoff      = 0.01
    ),
    error = function(e) NULL
  )

  if (!is.null(l_edge)) {
    out_file <- file.path(output_gsea,
                          paste0("NanoTube_GSEA_", stim, ".xlsx"))
    tryCatch(
      fgseaPostprocessingXLSX(
        genesetResults = gsea_res[["VisitW16"]],
        leadingEdge    = l_edge,
        limmaResults   = limma_fits[[stim]],
        join.threshold = 0.5,
        filename       = out_file
      ),
      error = function(e) message("Postprocessing failed: ", e$message)
    )
    cat(sprintf("  Saved: %s\n", basename(out_file)))
  }

  n_sig <- sum(!is.na(gsea_res[["VisitW16"]]$padj) &
                 gsea_res[["VisitW16"]]$padj < 0.01, na.rm = TRUE)
  cat(sprintf("  Significant pathways (FDR < 0.01): %d\n", n_sig))
}

16 NanoTube bubble plot

Pathways are ordered by ascending FDR. Hallmark pathway names are prefixed with Hallmark to distinguish them from NanoString panel annotations.

if (nrow(nanotube_sig) > 0) {

  nanotube_sig_plot <- nanotube_sig %>%
    mutate(
      pathway_short = ifelse(
        grepl("^HALLMARK_", pathway),
        paste0("Hallmark: ", gsub("_", " ", gsub("^HALLMARK_", "", pathway))),
        gsub("_", " ", pathway)
      ),
      Stimulation = factor(Stimulation,
                           levels = c("Null", "Mtb_Ag", "LPS", "IL1B"))
    )

  pathway_order_nt <- nanotube_sig_plot %>%
    arrange(padj) %>%
    pull(pathway_short) %>%
    unique()

  nanotube_sig_plot <- nanotube_sig_plot %>%
    mutate(pathway_short = factor(pathway_short, levels = pathway_order_nt))

  p_3c <- ggplot(
      nanotube_sig_plot,
      aes(x = pathway_short, y = Stimulation,
          size = -log10(padj), color = NES)
    ) +
    geom_point(alpha = 0.8) +
    scale_color_gradient2(
      low      = "blue",
      mid      = "white",
      high     = "red",
      midpoint = 0,
      name     = "NES"
    ) +
    scale_size_continuous(range = c(3, 10), name = "-log10(FDR)") +
    scale_x_discrete(drop = FALSE) +
    scale_y_discrete(drop = FALSE) +
    labs(
      title    = "Pathway enrichment: W16 vs W0",
      subtitle = "NanoString panel annotations and Hallmark | Paired limma, FDR < 0.01 | Red: higher at W16 | Blue: higher at W0",
      x        = "Pathway",
      y        = "Stimulation"
    ) +
    theme_classic(base_size = 12) +
    theme(
      axis.text.x      = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, color = "black", size = 9),
      axis.text.y      = element_text(color = "black"),
      panel.grid.major = element_line(color = "gray90"),
      legend.position  = "right"
    )

  print(p_3c)

  ggsave(
    file.path(output_fig3c, "3C_NanoTube_bubble_plot.pdf"),
    plot   = p_3c,
    width  = 12,
    height = 6,
    units  = "in"
  )
}

17 PLAGE validation function

run_plage_paired: for each pathway, the expression matrix of pathway genes is mean-centred and decomposed by SVD. The first right singular vector gives a pathway activity score per sample. The sign is corrected so that a higher score corresponds to higher mean pathway expression. A paired t-test compares W0 and W16 scores matched by donor. PLAGE uses combined NanoString and Hallmark pathway set for the validation, keeping it methodologically distinct from the primary analysis.

run_plage_paired <- function(data, stimulation, pathway_name, gene_set,
                              visit_pair = c("W0", "W16")) {

  available_genes <- intersect(gene_set, names(data))
  if (length(available_genes) < 3) return(NULL)

  stim_data <- data %>%
    filter(Stimulation == stimulation, Visit %in% visit_pair)

  paired_donors <- stim_data %>%
    group_by(Donor) %>%
    summarise(
      has_v1 = any(Visit == visit_pair[1]),
      has_v2 = any(Visit == visit_pair[2]),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) %>%
    filter(has_v1 & has_v2) %>%
    pull(Donor)

  if (length(paired_donors) < 3) return(NULL)

  expr_data <- stim_data %>%
    filter(Donor %in% paired_donors) %>%
    arrange(Donor, Visit)

  expr_mat      <- t(as.matrix(expr_data[, available_genes]))
  expr_mat      <- expr_mat - rowMeans(expr_mat)
  svd_res       <- svd(expr_mat)
  sample_scores <- svd_res$v[, 1]

  if (cor(sample_scores, colMeans(expr_mat)) < 0) {
    sample_scores <- -sample_scores
  }

  expr_data$score <- sample_scores

  w0  <- expr_data %>% filter(Visit == visit_pair[1]) %>% arrange(Donor)
  w16 <- expr_data %>% filter(Visit == visit_pair[2]) %>% arrange(Donor)

  common_donors <- intersect(w0$Donor, w16$Donor)
  s0  <- w0$score[match(common_donors, w0$Donor)]
  s16 <- w16$score[match(common_donors, w16$Donor)]

  test <- tryCatch(
    t.test(s16, s0, paired = TRUE),
    error = function(e) NULL
  )

  if (is.null(test)) return(NULL)

  data.frame(
    Pathway     = pathway_name,
    Stimulation = stimulation,
    N_genes     = length(available_genes),
    N_pairs     = length(common_donors),
    Score_diff  = mean(s16 - s0),
    t_statistic = as.numeric(test$statistic),
    P_value     = test$p.value,
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
}

18 Run PLAGE for all stimulations (validation)

plage_results <- list()

for (stim in stimulations) {
  results <- bind_rows(lapply(names(combined_pathways), function(pw) {
    run_plage_paired(
      data          = nano_data_resid,
      stimulation   = stim,
      pathway_name  = pw,
      gene_set      = combined_pathways[[pw]]
    )
  }))

  if (!is.null(results) && nrow(results) > 0) {
    results <- results %>%
      mutate(P_adj = p.adjust(P_value, method = "fdr")) %>%
      arrange(P_adj)

    plage_results[[stim]] <- results

    cat(sprintf(
      "%s: %d pathways tested | FDR < 0.01: %d\n | FDR < 0.01: %d\n",
      stim,
      nrow(results),
      sum(results$P_adj < 0.01, na.rm = TRUE),
      sum(results$P_adj < 0.01, na.rm = TRUE)
    ))
  }
}

19 PLAGE validation bubble plot

if (nrow(sig_plage) > 0) {

  pathway_order_plage <- sig_plage %>%
    arrange(P_adj) %>%
    pull(Pathway) %>%
    unique()

  plage_plot_data <- sig_plage %>%
    mutate(
      Pathway     = factor(Pathway, levels = pathway_order_plage),
      Stimulation = factor(Stimulation,
                           levels = c("Null", "Mtb_Ag", "LPS", "IL1B"))
    )

  p_plage <- ggplot(
      plage_plot_data,
      aes(x = Pathway, y = Stimulation,
          size = -log10(P_adj), color = Score_diff)
    ) +
    geom_point(alpha = 0.8) +
    scale_color_gradient2(
      low      = "blue",
      mid      = "white",
      high     = "red",
      midpoint = 0,
      name     = "Score difference\n(W16 minus W0)"
    ) +
    scale_size_continuous(range = c(3, 10), name = "-log10(FDR)") +
    scale_x_discrete(drop = FALSE) +
    scale_y_discrete(drop = FALSE) +
    labs(
      title    = "Pathway activity changes: W16 vs W0 (PLAGE validation)",
      subtitle = "NanoString panel annotations | Paired t-test, FDR < 0.01 | Red: higher at W16 | Blue: higher at W0",
      x        = "Pathway",
      y        = "Stimulation"
    ) +
    theme_classic(base_size = 12) +
    theme(
      axis.text.x      = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, color = "black", size = 9),
      axis.text.y      = element_text(color = "black"),
      panel.grid.major = element_line(color = "gray90"),
      legend.position  = "right"
    )

  print(p_plage)

  ggsave(
    file.path(output_fig3c, "3C_PLAGE_validation_bubble_plot.pdf"),
    plot   = p_plage,
    width  = 30,
    height = 6,
    units  = "in"
  )
}

20 Cross-validation: pathways significant in both analyses

Pathways that are significant in both the NanoTube primary analysis and the PLAGE validation are the most robust findings. Only NanoString-defined pathways are compared here since PLAGE uses NanoString annotations only.

nanotube_nanostring_sig <- nanotube_sig %>%
  select(pathway, Stimulation, NES, padj) %>%
  rename(NanoTube_NES = NES, NanoTube_padj = padj)

plage_sig_long <- sig_plage %>%
  select(Pathway, Stimulation, Score_diff, P_adj) %>%
  rename(
    pathway        = Pathway,
    PLAGE_Score_diff = Score_diff,
    PLAGE_padj       = P_adj
  )

confirmed <- inner_join(
  nanotube_nanostring_sig,
  plage_sig_long,
  by = c("pathway", "Stimulation")
) %>%
  arrange(NanoTube_padj)

cat(sprintf(
  "Pathways significant in both NanoTube and PLAGE: %d\n",
  nrow(confirmed)
))

21 Figure 3C: Cross-validation bubble plot

22 Shows only pathways significant in both NanoTube and PLAGE.

23 Bubble size reflects NanoTube FDR. Colour reflects NanoTube NES direction.

24 A separate score difference column from PLAGE is shown as a secondary label.

if (nrow(confirmed) > 0) {

  confirmed_plot <- confirmed %>%
    mutate(
      pathway_short = ifelse(
        grepl("^HALLMARK_", pathway),
        paste0("Hallmark: ", gsub("_", " ", gsub("^HALLMARK_", "", pathway))),
        gsub("_", " ", pathway)
      ),
      Stimulation = factor(Stimulation,
                           levels = c("Null", "Mtb_Ag", "LPS", "IL1B"))
    )

  pathway_order_confirmed <- confirmed_plot %>%
    arrange(NanoTube_padj) %>%
    pull(pathway_short) %>%
    unique()

  confirmed_plot <- confirmed_plot %>%
    mutate(pathway_short = factor(pathway_short, levels = pathway_order_confirmed))

  p_confirmed <- ggplot(
      confirmed_plot,
      aes(x = pathway_short, y = Stimulation,
          size = -log10(NanoTube_padj), color = NanoTube_NES)
    ) +
    geom_point(alpha = 0.8) +
    scale_color_gradient2(
      low      = "blue",
      mid      = "white",
      high     = "red",
      midpoint = 0,
      name     = "NES\n(NanoTube)"
    ) +
    scale_size_continuous(range = c(3, 10), name = "-log10(FDR)\n(NanoTube)") +
    scale_x_discrete(drop = FALSE) +
    scale_y_discrete(drop = FALSE) +
    labs(
      title    = "Significant pathways in NanoTube and PLAGE | NanoString immune panel and Hallmark",
      subtitle = "Cross-validated results | FDR < 0.01 in both analyses | Red: higher at W16; Blue: higher at W0",
      x        = "Pathway",
      y        = "Stimulation"
    ) +
    theme_classic(base_size = 12) +
    theme(
      axis.text.x      = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, color = "black", size = 9),
      axis.text.y      = element_text(color = "black"),
      panel.grid.major = element_line(color = "gray90"),
      legend.position  = "right"
    )

  print(p_confirmed)

  ggsave(
    file.path(output_fig3c, "3C_Confirmed_pathways_bubble_plot.pdf"),
    plot   = p_confirmed,
    width  = 10,
    height = 6,
    units  = "in"
  )

} else {
  cat("No pathways confirmed in both analyses. No plot generated.\n")
}
